Previous PCR studies on dairy cattle in the North Kazakhstan have identified C. parvum and C. andersoni as a prevalent species, and C. parvum was particularly significant in young calves, while C. andersoni was more common in older animals. These findings highlight the importance of understanding the prevalence and transmission of Cryptosporidium species in dairy farming for both animal health and potential zoonotic risks. In Germany, the prevalence of C. parvum in calves ranges from 21.5 to 44.0%, which is comparable to the results of this study. Globally, prevalence rates of Cryptosporidium spp. in calves range from 6.2 to 100%. The age-specific distribution in our findings, with the highest detection rate (66.7%) in calves aged 8–14 days, is consistent with previous research. Furthermore, the absence of seasonal variation in the risk of Cryptosporidium infection also aligns with findings from other studies.
answer: Cryptosporidium spp. was the most common pathogen detected in dairy calves, with 35.1% prevalence and most infections occurring in animals under 30 days old, suggesting likely C. parvum infection. The highest detection rate was 66.7% in calves aged 8–14 days, with no seasonal variation; these patterns align with prior studies and emphasize the animal-health and zoonotic importance of Cryptosporidium transmission in dairy farming.

query: The results of this study provide an in-depth understanding of the diet of tigers in the national park and the buffer zone area, which explicitly relied on wild prey, while the tiger population was recovering in Nepal. The tiger was maximizing its hunting efficiency by targeting solitary, medium-sized prey such as hog deer and wild boar for their easy availability and muscular biomass. Thus, park authorities should focus on the conservation of not only large prey but also medium-sized prey for long-term tiger conservation to accommodate more tigers up to their ecological carrying capacity and reduce the risk of livestock predation. However, the findings extracted from small scat samples of the confirmed tiger scats for DNA metabarcoding (n = 58), particularly in the buffer zone (n = 20), collected in only one season (dry period) of the year might not represent the broader prey assemblage of the area (both natural and domestic). Literature suggests that the minimum value needed for comparative analysis would be \~90 scat samples. As only a few individual tigers (< 5% of the population) are involved in conflict, and the park authority proactively captures the conflict-causing tigers, we might miss the scats of those tigers. Furthermore, the limited samples might result in a low frequency of occurrences of larger prey like sambar, and this may also be due to its lower density than spotted deer in the area. We recommend further study with more sample sizes, capturing both seasons (dry and wet) of the year, which may yield a better understanding of the tiger's diet composition in the area. Even collecting scats from outside of the protected areas (from the corridor) may also provide insight into the diet of the dispersing tigers.
answer: The study found that recovering tiger populations in Nepal's national park and buffer zone relied on wild prey, especially solitary medium-sized species such as hog deer and wild boar, suggesting that conservation should protect both large and medium-sized prey to support more tigers and reduce livestock predation risk. The findings are limited by a small, dry-season scat sample for DNA metabarcoding (58 confirmed tiger scats, including 20 from the buffer zone), below the roughly 90 samples suggested for comparative analysis, and may have missed conflict-causing tigers, larger prey such as sambar, wet-season diets, and dispersing tigers outside protected areas.

query: Animals are exposed to leptospira when contaminated water or food containing urine from an infected host-adapted species enter the body via the mucous membranes or skin lesions. In horses, leptospiral exposure is common following heavy rains or flooding in which horses are exposed to stagnant water. Leptospiral infections in horses have been associated with abortion, acute renal failure, and neonatal disease, but most commonly, horses develop transient fever, malaise, and jaundice, which are rarely observed or reported. Thus, signs of acute disease are primarily subclinical. However, uveitis has been reported to develop in horses up to 24 months after acute infection with leptospira. In one report of natural exposure and disease in which L. Pomona was isolated, horses developed uveitis 18–24 months after signs of acute leptospirosis. In another study, a group of ponies with experimentally-induced L. interrogans serogroup Pomona infection developed ocular inflammation in 61% of eyes within 15 months of the initial leptospiral exposure.
answer: Horses acquire leptospira when contaminated water or food containing urine from infected host-adapted species enters through mucous membranes or skin lesions, especially after heavy rains or flooding with stagnant water exposure. Equine leptospiral infection is linked to abortion, acute renal failure, neonatal disease, and usually subclinical acute signs such as transient fever, malaise, and jaundice, but uveitis can develop months later. Reported ocular disease occurred 18–24 months after natural L. Pomona leptospirosis, and experimentally induced L. interrogans serogroup Pomona infection caused ocular inflammation in 61% of pony eyes within 15 months.

query: Kazakhstan is the ninth largest country in the world, with more than 180 million hectares of pasture land, of which only 45% is used for its intended purpose. Due to the rearing of animals on permanently restricted contaminated pasture areas, infestation of animals with invasive elements occurs. Sarcocystosis is of epidemiological importance as it is dangerous for humans. The consumption of horse meat in food is part of the national character; the local people consume a lot of horse meat. A person consuming insufficiently cooked meat becomes infected with the cysts of the parasite, resulting in intestinal sarcocystosis. The pathogen, by invading and parasitising the tissues of vital organs, releases sarcotoxin and poses a threat to human and animal health. To date, it is not known how many species of Sarcocystis can infect the horse. The horse is an intermediate host of the highly pathogenic species S.neurona, which causes central nervous system disease and specifically causes the protozoal disease equine myeloencephalitis.
answer: Sarcocystosis is epidemiologically important in Kazakhstan because extensive but restricted contaminated pastures can expose livestock, and horse meat is commonly consumed. Humans can develop intestinal sarcocystosis after eating insufficiently cooked meat containing parasite cysts, while Sarcocystis parasites can invade vital tissues, release sarcotoxin, and threaten human and animal health. Horses are intermediate hosts for the highly pathogenic S.neurona, which causes central nervous system disease and equine protozoal myeloencephalitis.

query: The FoxO transcription factors constitute a vital protein family regulating various biological processes, such as cell cycle progression, apoptosis. Activation of the FoxO signaling pathway plays a pivotal role in maintaining metabolic homeostasis. Exposure to high environmental ammonia in grass carp significantly alters the FoxO signaling pathway, which induces oxidative stress. Similarly, under hypoxic conditions, crucian carp (Carassius auratus) exhibit significant enrichment of upregulated genes in the FoxO signaling pathway. In turbot, thermal stress enhances key hub genes in the FoxO signaling pathway. The findings from the current project suggested that $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ activated FoxO signaling via upregulation of IRS, AMPK, and SGK, subsequently increasing expression of BNIP3, Gadd45, and Atrogin-1, ultimately triggering muscle autophagy, oxidative stress, and DNA damage. Our findings corroborated this stressresponse paradigm, demonstrating that $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$ -induced oxidative stress upregulates foxo3 expression along with its downstream targets (BNIP3, Gadd45, and Atrogin-1) in carp muscle. Notably, oxidative stress can upregulate BNIP3 expression, thereby activating autophagy and exerting cytoprotective effects. Additionally, Gadd45 is primarily involved in biological processes such as cell cycle regulation, oxidative stress response, and apoptosis. Therefore, we reasonably hypothesize that the upregulation of these related genes triggers protective mechanisms to counteract oxidative stress.
answer: FoxO transcription factors regulate processes including cell cycle progression, apoptosis, and metabolic homeostasis, and their signaling is altered by stressors in fish such as ammonia in grass carp, hypoxia in crucian carp, and heat in turbot. In common carp muscle, $\mathrm { H } _ { 2 } \mathrm { O } _ { 2 }$-induced oxidative stress activated FoxO signaling by upregulating IRS, AMPK, SGK, foxo3, and downstream targets BNIP3, Gadd45, and Atrogin-1, linked to autophagy, oxidative stress, DNA damage, and possible protective responses.

query: A critical aspect associated with embryonic development is oxidation which strongly relates to some vitamins (mainly C and E) and minerals (mainly Selenium). The chicken embryo is very sensitive to oxidative stress due to the release of ROS during β-oxidation of PUFA, the main energy source during embryogenesis. The level of yolk antioxidants has been associated with the rate of embryonic develop ment. In ovo administration of Vitamin E was not effective, while Vitamin C and Arg seemed to improve antioxidant status as measured through malondialdehyde (MDA) superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione (GSH). Moreover, IOF of vitamin E in turkey and broiler embryos enhanced humoral and cellular immune system components at the expense of reducing hatchability at high doses (above 10 IU) in turkeys. In addition, vitamin D3 (25-hydrox ycholecalciferol), improved bone development and folic acid changed plasma metabolomic profiles including P, glucose, and cholesterol together with increased body weight at hatch. The main highlight on trace minerals supplementation has been around selenium. The IOF of sodium selenite injection has been associated with positive results around increasing the resilience against challenges with Clostridium perfringens and coccidiosis (Eimeria maxima), improving immune response (increasing IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8 and antibody titres) and antioxidant status. Other mineral IOF around organic forms of Zn, Mn, and copper have identified potential limitations with adverse effects on hatchability and growth, but also potential opportunities on bone mineralisation improvement (reviewed by Peebles).
answer: Chicken embryos are highly sensitive to oxidative stress because ROS are released during β-oxidation of PUFA, their main embryonic energy source, and yolk antioxidant levels are linked to developmental rate. In ovo Vitamin C and Arg improved antioxidant markers, whereas Vitamin E was ineffective in chickens and high-dose Vitamin E above 10 IU reduced hatchability in turkeys despite enhancing immune components. Selenium, especially sodium selenite injection, improved resistance to Clostridium perfringens and Eimeria maxima challenges, immune responses including IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8 and antibody titres, and antioxidant status, while organic Zn, Mn and copper may aid bone mineralisation but can impair hatchability and growth.

query: Enhancers are cis-regulatory elements that control spatiotemporal gene expression patterns. Super-enhancers (SEs). which function as clustered regulatory elements. play crucial roles in establishment and maintenance of cellular identity. Accumulating evidence highlights the importance of SEs in mammalian adipogenesis and fat deposition. However, adipocyte-specific SEs (ASSEs) in chicken adipose tissue have not been systematically characterized at the genome-wide level. In this study, we performed the Cleavage Under Targets and Tag mentation (CUT&Tag) profiling of H3K4me1, H3K27ac, and PPARγ binding in chicken adipose tissue. Integration of these three datasets led to the identification of 278 ASSEs. which were associated with 1.129 genes within ±100 kb window. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that these ASSE-associated genes (ASSEAGs) are implicated in key signaling pathways, including PI3K-Akt, PPAR, Hippo, and JAK-STAT. To evaluate the po tential role of ASSEs in chicken adipose tissue, we intersected the ASSEAGs with the differentially expressed genes from abdominal adipose tissues of the Northeast Agricultural University broiler lines divergently selected for abdominal fat content (NEAUHLF). This analysis identified 93 overlapping genes. Furthermore, transcription factor binding site enrichment analysis showed significant overrepresentation of binding sites for PPARγ, C/ EBPα, C/EBPβ, CTCF, EBF2, and KLFs within the ASSEs. Additionally, the identified ASSEs overlapped with 1,125 quantitative trait loci (QTLs) related to various chicken traits. Collectively, our findings provide a comprehensive characterization of chicken ASSEs and offer new insights into the regulatory mechanisms un derlying adipogenesis and adipose tissue development in chickens.
answer: Chicken adipocyte-specific super-enhancers (ASSEs) were characterized genome-wide using CUT&Tag profiling of H3K4me1, H3K27ac, and PPARγ binding in adipose tissue. The integrated analysis identified 278 ASSEs associated with 1.129 nearby genes, enriched for PI3K-Akt, PPAR, Hippo, and JAK-STAT pathways; 93 of these genes overlapped differentially expressed genes between NEAUHLF fat and lean broiler lines. ASSEs were enriched for binding sites of PPARγ, C/EBPα, C/EBPβ, CTCF, EBF2, and KLFs and overlapped 1,125 chicken trait QTLs, suggesting roles in adipogenesis and adipose tissue development.

query: All Chlamydia are obligate intracellular parasites, possessing unique biphasic life characteristics. They are capable of overcoming numerous obstacles, such as entering host cells, persisting and reproducing within host cells, and surviving in harsh extracellular environments. Two forms that are different in both function and appearance will alternate in a certain sequence. The elementary body (EB) is infectious and in a metabolic quiescent state, responsible for attaching to the target host cell and facilitating its entry into the cell; while the reticular body (RB) is an unfinished, non-infectious and metabolically active intracellular form, which replicates by binary fission and is reorganized into the basic body before being released through cell cycle. However, the pathogenic core of C. psittaci lies in the host immunopathological response it triggers, rather than direct cytotoxicity. The severity of the disease is closely related to excessive natural immune responses, imbalances in T cell reactions, such as Th1/Th17 types, and associated cytokine storms. Therefore, an ideal animal model must be capable of accurately replicating this complex immune network, so as to study the balance mechanism between the protective clearance function of the immune system and its destructive responses.
answer: Chlamydia are obligate intracellular parasites with a biphasic life cycle: infectious, metabolically quiescent elementary bodies attach to and enter host cells, while noninfectious, metabolically active reticular bodies replicate intracellularly before reorganizing for release. For C. psittaci, disease is driven mainly by host immunopathological responses rather than direct cytotoxicity, with severity linked to excessive innate immunity, Th1/Th17 T-cell imbalance, and cytokine storms. Effective animal models must reproduce this immune network to study the balance between protective clearance and destructive immune responses.

query: There is currently no licensed antiviral therapy or human vaccine approved for the treatment or prevention of NiV infection. Clinical management, therefore, remains largely supportive, with outcomes strongly influenced by early recognition, rapid initiation of appropriate care, and rigorous IPC measures. Observational data from outbreak settings indicate that timely access to intensive supportive care may be associated with improved survival, although these findings are subject to confounding factors, including differences in disease severity and access to healthcare. NiV infection most commonly presents as acute encephalitis, severe respiratory disease, or a combination of both, often following a short prodromal phase characterised by non-specific febrile illness, headache, and myalgia. Clinical deterioration may be rapid, underscoring the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion in patients with compatible exposure histories. Early clinical management priorities prompt isola tion of suspected cases, comprehensive neurological assessment, and close monitoring for signs of raised intracranial pressure, seizures, and altered consciousness. Seizure control, airway protection, and haemo dynamic stabilisation are central components of early care. Res piratory involvement ranges from mild pneumonia to fulminant acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), requiring escalating levels of oxygen therapy and, in severe cases, invasive mechanical ventilation. Supportive management includes lung-protective ventilation strategies and careful fluid management, balanced against the need to maintain cerebral perfusion in patients with concurrent neurological disease. Multiorgan dysfunction has been reported in severe cases, necessitating coordinated critical care support. Overall, clinical management of Nipah virus infection largely follows established prin ciples for the treatment of viral encephalitis and acute respiratory distress syndrome. The primary added value in the context of NiV lies in early recognition and the timely implementation of IPC measures to prevent secondary transmission in healthcare settings.
answer: Nipah virus infection has no licensed antiviral treatment or approved human vaccine, so care is mainly supportive and depends on early recognition, rapid clinical management, and strict infection prevention and control. Disease commonly presents as acute encephalitis, severe respiratory disease, or both after a short febrile prodrome, and management focuses on isolation, neurological monitoring, seizure control, airway and hemodynamic support, lung-protective ventilation, careful fluids, and coordinated critical care for severe multiorgan disease.

query: Synchronization protocols play a crucial role in improving reproductive efficiency in dairy herds by enhancing the timing and success of artificial insemination. Their impact on pregnancy rates is significant, particularly in high producing cows where fertility tends to be compromised. In this study, a comprehensive comparison of four estrus synchronization and insemination protocols was conducted, assessing both reproductive performance and economic efficiency. The results demonstrate that the Double Ovsynch protocol, especially when used with a single, well-timed insemination, offers the greatest reproductive advantage. Group DOV1, which followed this approach, achieved the highest pregnancy rate (64.8%) and the lowest cost per confirmed pregnancy (EUR 89.51), identifying it as the most efficient strategy based on both biological and economic outcomes.
answer: In dairy herds, estrus synchronization protocols improve reproductive efficiency by improving the timing and success of artificial insemination, especially in high-producing cows with compromised fertility. In a comparison of four synchronization and insemination protocols, Double Ovsynch with a single well-timed insemination was the most effective and economical approach, with Group DOV1 achieving the highest pregnancy rate (64.8%) and the lowest cost per confirmed pregnancy (EUR 89.51).

query: In this context, our study aims to leverage data from intra-ruminal bolus sensors and the DeLeval DelPro system, which together provide continuous measurements of core physiological parameters such as internal body temperature, activity, rumination behavior, water intake, and production metrics. These internal sensor streams will be complemented by thermal imaging data acquired through automated heat cameras installed in the milking station, enabling contactless monitoring of udder and limb temperature patterns associated with inflammation. By integrating these physiological, thermal, and environmental signals into a unified multimodal AI framework, we seek to identify early deviations from normal health trajectories and detect early-stage health disorders, specifically mastitis and infections affecting the udder, hoof, and leg. In this study, “early” disease detection is defined operationally as the identification of abnormal physiological, production, or thermal patterns during the incubation period preceding veterinarian-confirmed diagnosis and treatment. Based on veterinary records, this period was defined as up to 20 days before clinical intervention, allowing the model to target subclinical and preclinical stages of disease. This approach offers the potential for earlier interventions, improved welfare outcomes, and more efficient herd management compared with traditional single-modality or wearable-only monitoring systems.
answer: The study integrates intra-ruminal bolus and DeLeval DelPro data on body temperature, activity, rumination, water intake, and production with automated thermal imaging of udder and limb temperatures in a multimodal AI framework. It aims to detect early deviations linked to mastitis and udder, hoof, and leg infections, defining early detection as abnormal physiological, production, or thermal patterns up to 20 days before veterinarian-confirmed diagnosis and treatment.

query: Furthermore, water intake increases as a strategy to cool the body and replenish fluids through elevated respiratory activity and perspiration. In adult animals, heat stress has been associated with increased insulin concentrations and decreased thyroid hormones due to altered cellular energy metabolism. In calves, heat stress leads to reduced feed intake and performance, as a result of metabolic energy partitioning. Heat stress also reduces gastrointestinal motility, alters ruminal microbiota, slows the passage rate, decreases digestibility, and impairs nutrient absorption due to diminished blood flow. Moreover, in utero heat stress has been shown to have postnatal consequences, including reduced neonatal body and immune organ weights, increased jejunal enterocyte apoptosis, and delayed physical and immune system development. Dairy calves subjected to early heat stress, even with post-pubertal weight gain recovery, exhibit a metabolic shift and fail to achieve optimal development.
answer: Heat stress increases water intake to support cooling and fluid replacement and is associated in adult animals with higher insulin and lower thyroid hormone concentrations. In calves, it reduces feed intake and performance, disrupts gastrointestinal motility, ruminal microbiota, passage rate, digestibility, and nutrient absorption, while in utero exposure can impair neonatal body and immune organ development. Early heat stress in dairy calves may cause lasting metabolic shifts and prevent optimal development even if weight gain later recovers.

query: In the present study, astaxanthin supplementation administered through milk replacer did not affect growth performance in preweaning Holstein calves, as body weight and average daily gain were maintained throughout the experimental period. However, astaxanthin-supplemented calves exhibited a lower frequency of diarrhea episodes, which may suggest a beneficial effect on gastrointestinal health that was not fully captured by growth-related parameters alone. The reduction in diarrhea incidence was accompanied by changes in fecal bacterial populations, including lower coliform counts and higher total bacterial counts toward the end of the trial, which may indicate a modulation of selected components of the gut microbial environment rather than a generalized antimicrobial effect. Clinical health indicators and rectal temperature were not adversely affected by treatment, supporting the overall tolerability of astaxanthin supplementation during early life. Treatment-related differences observed in selected serum metabolic parameters, remained within physiological ranges and are more likely attributable to age-related developmental processes and early-life variability than to direct effects of astaxanthin. Overall, these findings suggest that astaxanthin supplementation could be associated with improved gastrointestinal health in preweaning calves without negatively affecting growth performance. Given the exploratory nature of the study, the limited sample size, and the reliance on culture-based microbiological methods, further research using larger cohorts and comprehensive microbiota and functional analyses is required to confirm these results and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of action. Nevertheless, the reduction in diarrhea incidence and the associated changes in fecal bacterial populations provide promising evidence that astaxanthin supplementation may support gastrointestinal health in preweaning calves.
answer: Astaxanthin given through milk replacer to preweaning Holstein calves did not change body weight or average daily gain, and it did not adversely affect clinical health indicators or rectal temperature. Supplemented calves had fewer diarrhea episodes, with lower fecal coliform counts and higher total bacterial counts toward the end of the trial, suggesting selective modulation of the gut microbial environment rather than broad antimicrobial activity. Serum metabolic differences stayed within physiological ranges, and larger studies with more comprehensive microbiota analyses are needed to confirm the gastrointestinal health effects.

query: In our study, Campylobacterota and Campylobacter were found to be more abundant in pre-calving faecal samples of dairy cows than in post-calving samples. We did not identify any particular species or strains. As a result, we cannot determine whether the identifed shifts in Campylobacter were for commensal or pathogenic bacteria. Campylobacter has been thoroughly studied, as it poses a risk to human health, by causing campylobacteriosis, a gastrointestinal infection. In 2022, campylobacterosis was identifed as the frst foodborne zoonosis, and associated with contaminated poultry and cattle products. While some Campylobacter species (e.g., C. jejuni) are of zoonotic concern, others like Campylobacter lanienae are commonly found in ruminants without causing overt disease in the animals, but might be of human concern. Campylobacter fetus is also known to cause venereal campylobacteriosis in ruminants, afecting fertility and causing on-farm abortions.
answer: Campylobacterota and Campylobacter were more abundant in dairy cow fecal samples before calving than after calving, but species or strains were not identified, so the shifts could not be classified as commensal or pathogenic. Campylobacter is important because it can cause human campylobacteriosis, was identified in 2022 as the leading foodborne zoonosis linked to contaminated poultry and cattle products, includes zoonotic species such as C. jejuni, ruminant-associated C. lanienae, and C. fetus, which causes venereal campylobacteriosis, infertility, and abortions in ruminants.

query: The prevalence of cardiac arrhythmias in sick goats has not been reported previously. One study described cardiac arrhythmias in clinically healthy goats in Iran. In that study, only 0.5% of healthy goats had an arrhythmia considered to be abnormal (atrial [supraventricular] premature complexes). No other studies have described the frequency of arrhythmias in healthy or medically ill goats, and the clinical relevance of many arrhythmias in goats is not well understood. In our study, approximately one-third of all goats had ventricular arrhythmias noted, including healthy goats. Ventricular ectopic activity has been identified in healthy humans and animals. Although no data exist in goats, one ventricular ectopic beat per hour can be seen in normal horses, and this number is considered clinically unimportant if the abnormal beats disappear with exercise. The number of VPDs noted in the healthy goats and the majority of the medically ill goats would be considered within the range of normal for other species, with only 2 medically ill goats having frequent VPDs considered outside the range of normal for other species (up to 200 in a 24-h period). Ventricular arrhythmias that are complex (couplets, triplets, bigeminy or trigeminy patterns, R-on-T, multiform ventricular tachycardia) are cause for greater clinical concern; 4 goats in our study were noted to have ventricular couplets, 2 of which also were found to have a ventricular rhythm consistent with AIVR or VT. Additionally, although underlying structural heart disease worsens prognosis in horses, the exact number of VPDs in horses above which the risk of sudden death increases remains unknown. Given the fact that a single VPD with early coupling could lead to R-on-T, a safe number of VPDs is difficult to predict, and rather a consideration of the acceptable risk for a species (including goats) should be considered.
answer: Cardiac arrhythmia prevalence in sick goats had not previously been reported, and prior data in healthy goats found abnormal arrhythmias in only 0.5%. In this study, about one-third of goats, including healthy animals, had ventricular arrhythmias; most ventricular premature depolarizations were within ranges considered normal in other species, but 2 medically ill goats had frequent VPDs up to 200 in 24 hours. Complex ventricular arrhythmias are more concerning: 4 goats had ventricular couplets, 2 of which also had rhythms consistent with accelerated idioventricular rhythm or ventricular tachycardia, making a universally safe number of VPDs difficult to define.

query: Acute respiratory distress is a common reason for dogs to present to emergency services, accounting for 16% of emergency visits in dogs in a large-scale study. Acute respiratory distress may arise from a broad range of respiratory, cardiovascular, and noncardiopulmonary disorders. However, respiratory distress accompanied by hemoptysis is an uncommon presentation in dogs. Hemoptysis, defined as bleeding originating from the lower respiratory tract, carries a wide differential diagnosis. In dogs presenting with hemoptysis, the most commonly reported underlying causes in a retrospective study of 36 cases identified during a 10-year period at a university teaching hospital were bacterial bronchopneumonia (19.4%), respiratory neoplasia (13.9%), and trauma (13.9%), followed by systemic causes such as heartworm disease (11.1%) and immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (11.1%). Additional reported etiologies associated with hemoptysis or pulmonary hemorrhage include structural or iatrogenic factors (e.g., lung lobe torsion, airway foreign bodies, or bronchoscopic biopsy), intoxications (most notably anticoagulant rodenticides), specific infectious agents (e.g., leptospirosis, aspergillosis, or pneumonic plague), and seizure-associated events.
answer: Acute respiratory distress accounts for 16% of canine emergency visits, but respiratory distress with hemoptysis, bleeding from the lower respiratory tract, is uncommon and has many possible causes. In a 36-dog retrospective study, the most common causes of hemoptysis were bacterial bronchopneumonia (19.4%), respiratory neoplasia (13.9%), trauma (13.9%), heartworm disease (11.1%), and immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (11.1%), with other causes including structural or iatrogenic lesions, anticoagulant rodenticide intoxication, infections such as leptospirosis, aspergillosis, or pneumonic plague, and seizure-associated events.

query: Canine leishmaniosis, caused by Leishmania infantum, is a vector-borne disease in which early treatment monitoring remains challenging. This prospective study evaluated short-term changes in serological, inflammatory, and serum protein electrophoretic parameters during first-line therapy with meglumine antimoniate plus allopurinol. Eighteen dogs with confirmed clinical disease were enrolled at diagnosis, and fifteen dogs completing all follow-up visits (Days 0, 7, 14, 21, and 29) were included. Infection was confirmed by compatible clinical and/or laboratory abnormalities, high anti-Leishmania antibody levels, and successful parasite isolation. Anti-Leishmania antibodies were quantified using in-house single-dilution and two-fold serial dilution ELISA; circulating immune complexes, C-reactive protein, a complete blood count, a biochemical profile, and serum protein electrophoresis were also assessed. Both ELISA methods showed a signifi cant decline in antibody levels during treatment, with serial dilution ELISA showing greater discrimination among highly positive samples. C-reactive protein concentrations decreased significantly from diagnosis to Day 29, indicating reduced systemic inflammation. Serum protein electrophoresis showed significant increases in albumin and the albumin:globulin ratio, along with a significant decrease in gamma globulins. Circulating immune complexes concentrations remained stable. These findings support quantitative serology, C-reactive protein, and serum protein electrophoresis as useful tools for early monitoring of therapeutic response in clinical canine leishmaniosis.
answer: Canine leishmaniosis due to Leishmania infantum was monitored in a prospective study of dogs treated with meglumine antimoniate plus allopurinol, with 15 dogs completing follow-up from Day 0 to Day 29. Anti-Leishmania antibody levels declined significantly by both single-dilution and serial dilution ELISA, while C-reactive protein decreased, albumin and the albumin:globulin ratio increased, gamma globulins decreased, and circulating immune complexes remained stable. Quantitative serology, C-reactive protein, and serum protein electrophoresis may help monitor early therapeutic response in clinical canine leishmaniosis.

query: The identification of RESF1 as a causative gene for MAS represents a monogenic cause of autoimmune disease. The finding that a missense autosomal recessive variant can lead to AD in 76% of homozygous dogs highlights the important role RESF1 plays in immune regulation. These results support RESF1 as a potential mediator of autoimmune disease. Since identification of the RESF1 variant and its association with the juvenile-onset AD phenotype, a genetic test has been available to NSDTR breeders through UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/jadd-nsdtr). As a result, the frequency of the associated allele cannot be determined in NSDTR population. However, since implementation of genetic testing, no additional juvenileonset AD dogs from tested parents have been reported to our knowledge. The apparent elimination of the disease from the breed following the implementation of testing for this variant further supports the conclusion that the missense variant in RESF1 is the causative variant for MAS and juvenile-onset AD in the NSDTR breed. This work establishes RESF1 as a candidate gene for investigation in other autoimmune disease and provides insight into mechanisms of immune tolerance breakdown.
answer: RESF1 was identified as a causative gene for MAS, with a missense autosomal recessive variant leading to AD in 76% of homozygous dogs and supporting a role for RESF1 in immune regulation. A genetic test for NSDTR breeders has been available through UC Davis, and no additional juvenileonset AD dogs from tested parents have been reported, supporting the variant as causative for MAS and juvenile-onset AD in the breed.

query: Cardiovascular involvement in dogs with leishmaniosis have been recently reviewed. Myocardial involvement in canine leishmaniosis (CanL) has been documented through post-mortem histopathological evaluations of myocardial samples from infected/diseased dogs and by elevated levels of cardiac troponin I (cTnI). Such involvement occurs on an inflammatory basis, with predominantly lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory infiltrate. The mechanisms inducing cardiac injury and myocarditis are still under discussion; in particular, Leishmania spp. amastigotes in the muscle may act as a trigger for the inflammatory response, or muscle damage could be related to immunemediated mechanisms associated with the infection. In fact, antigenic characterisation studies of infiltrating mononuclear cells and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) I and II class expression in myocarditis associated with Leishmania infantum infection in dogs provide evidence that, during leishmaniosis, myocarditis can occur with morphological and immunophenotypic patterns similar to canine myositis associated with L. infantum infection. A study examining the hearts of 30 dogs infected with L. infantum chagasi found myocardial lesions in all dogs despite the parasite only being found in the cardiac tissue of 20/30 dogs. More recently, in a study of 31 dogs whose cardiac tissue were examined, most showed cardiac injuries, but amastigotes were detected in only one dog. Pericarditis associated with the presence of Leishmania spp. amastigotes in pericardial fluid have also been documented. However, studies evaluating the degree of myocardial dysfunction in affected dogs are currently limited.
answer: Canine leishmaniosis can involve the cardiovascular system, especially the myocardium, with inflammatory, predominantly lymphoplasmacytic lesions and sometimes elevated cardiac troponin I. Cardiac injury may be triggered by Leishmania spp. amastigotes in muscle or by infection-associated immune-mediated mechanisms, and myocarditis in L. infantum infection resembles canine myositis morphologically and immunophenotypically. Myocardial lesions have been reported even when parasites are absent or rarely detected in cardiac tissue, such as lesions in all 30 L. infantum chagasi-infected dogs despite parasites in only 20/30 hearts, and cardiac injuries in most of 31 dogs with amastigotes detected in only one.

query: Chronic enteropathies (CEs) are a group of disorders in dogs characterized by persistent or recurrent gastrointestinal signs such as diarrhea, vomiting, inappetence, weight loss, and abdominal pain. Among them, chronic inflammatory enteropathies are the most extensively studied and are hypothesized to result from an inappropriate immune response to dietary or microbial antigens in genetically susceptible dogs, although the exact mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Diagnosis relies on the exclusion of other causes of chronic gastrointestinal signs and on documenting a response to either dietary modification, microbiotatargeted interventions, or anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive treatment.
answer: Chronic enteropathies in dogs are disorders causing persistent or recurrent gastrointestinal signs, including diarrhea, vomiting, inappetence, weight loss, and abdominal pain. Chronic inflammatory enteropathies are thought to involve inappropriate immune responses to dietary or microbial antigens in genetically susceptible dogs, and diagnosis depends on excluding other causes and documenting response to diet, microbiota-targeted therapy, or anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive treatment.

query: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in dogs is a progressive condition with a poor prognosis and a lack of efective pharmacological interventions to extend survival. Beraprost, an oral prostacyclin analog approved for feline CKD, was of-label prescribed and evaluated for its efect on survival in dogs with naturally occurring IRIS stage 2 CKD. This prospective clinical study included a treatment group (n 16) receiving oral beraprost (12.5 μg/kg twice daily), and a well-matched historical control group (n 17) from the same institution. The primary outcome, overall survival, was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable between the groups. Significantly longer survival was observed in the beraprost-treated group, with a median survival time of 1,101 days (a 5.6-fold increase), compared to 198 days in the control group (P 0.001). Furthermore, beraprost therapy was associated with a significant delay in the time to secondary composite endpoints, including disease progression (to IRIS stage 3/4) or death (P 0.001) and 10% body weight loss or death (P 0.028), underscoring the robustness of the survival data. After adjusting for age and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, beraprost treatment remained the sole independent predictor of improved survival (hazard ratio, 0.15; 95% confidence interval 0.03–0.79; P 0.025). Although limited by its non-randomized design and small sample size, this study provides the first clinical evidence that oral beraprost is associated with a substantial benefit on overall survival in dogs with IRIS stage 2 CKD, supporting the need for large-scale randomized controlled trials.
answer: In dogs with naturally occurring IRIS stage 2 chronic kidney disease, off-label oral beraprost at 12.5 μg/kg twice daily was associated with markedly improved survival in a prospective study using a matched historical control group. Treated dogs had a median survival of 1,101 days versus 198 days in controls, delayed progression to IRIS stage 3/4 or death and 10% body weight loss or death, and beraprost remained the only independent predictor of improved survival after adjustment, though the study was limited by small size and non-randomized design.

query: The FMD clinical manifestation in pigs involves fever, depression, anorexia, and the formation of vesicles in the mouth, on the tongue, snout, and extremities, especially on the coronary band and interdigital cleft. Comparative studies of the domestic and wild pig susceptibility to FMDV A-24 Cruzeiro demonstrated that pigs were highly susceptible both to intradermal infection and contact infection due to the virus transmission from infected animals. In the domestic pigs, the FMD clinical signs developed in a shorter timeframe after contact with the diseased animals (24 h) compared with the wild pigs (48 h). Nevertheless, the dynamics of the virus accumulation and excretion were similar in both groups of animals, with maximum virus titer in oral swabs collected on days 2–4 post-infection.
answer: Foot-and-mouth disease in pigs causes fever, depression, anorexia, and vesicles in the mouth, tongue, snout, and extremities, especially the coronary band and interdigital cleft. Domestic and wild pigs were both highly susceptible to FMDV A-24 Cruzeiro by intradermal or contact infection, but domestic pigs developed signs sooner after contact exposure (24 h vs. 48 h), while both groups had similar virus accumulation and shedding with peak oral-swab titers on days 2–4 post-infection.

query: African swine fever was first identified in Kenya in 1921, initially occurring in countries south of the Sahara in Africa. The ASFV genotype I was first introduced from West Africa to Europe in 1960, marking the beginning of its spread beyond the African continent. In 2007, ASFV genotype II emerged from East Africa and rapidly spread across Europe, causing widespread outbreaks. In 2018, this virus strain was introduced into China and 10 other Asian countries. The consequences of an ASF outbreak in China have been catastrophic, both for the domestic economy and for international trade. On 3 August 2018, the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH) announced the initial detection of ASFV in Shenyang City, located in China’s Liaoning Province. The strain responsible for this outbreak belonged to genotype II. Despite the emergency measures implemented by the Chinese government, including strict quarantine and culling protocols, the ASFV outbreak subsequently spread rapidly to all 31 provincial-level administrative regions across the country. The virus strain was isolated and identified as genotype II, sharing high homology with the Georgia-07 strain, which is known to cause acute infections and is associated with 100% mortality in field pigs. With the prevalence of ASF in China, epidemiological surveillance of circulating strains in 2020 revealed the emergence of not only highly virulent genotype II strains but also low-virulence genotype II strains. Whole-genome sequencing indicated a deletion in the EP402R gene, which encodes the CD2v protein, resulting in the loss of hematopoietic adhesion capability in these lowvirulence strains. These low-virulence strains can cause mild mortality in pigs at high infectious doses, while at low doses they lead to persistent, non-fatal, subacute or chronic diseases. The long incubation period and high transmissibility of these low-virulence strains make early diagnosis more challenging.
answer: African swine fever virus (ASFV) was first identified in Kenya in 1921, with genotype I spreading from West Africa to Europe in 1960 and genotype II emerging from East Africa in 2007 before reaching China and 10 other Asian countries in 2018. China’s first reported outbreak occurred in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, on 3 August 2018 and involved a genotype II strain highly homologous to Georgia-07, associated with acute infection and 100% mortality in field pigs; it later spread to all 31 provincial-level regions despite quarantine and culling. By 2020, China had both highly virulent and low-virulence genotype II strains, including EP402R/CD2v-deleted variants that lose hematopoietic adhesion capability and can cause persistent, subacute or chronic disease with long incubation and high transmissibility, complicating early diagnosis.

query: The Swine Inflammation and Necrosis Syndrome (SINS) is a condition that combines clinical signs of inflammation and necrotic tissue in acral areas. It particularly afects the tail base and/or tip, ears, coronary bands, heels, sole, claw wall, teats, vulva, umbilicus, and face. This syndrome may be observed in suckling piglets with clinical signs being most evident during the first week of life, weaned and fattening pigs. Symptomatology generally begins with bristle loss, followed by swelling and redness, and in advanced stages, exudation, and necrosis. SINS as a primary endogenous disease has been associated to mycotoxins in feed, such as: zearalenone, deoxynivalenol, T-2, and ergot alkaloids. Other risk factors for the occurrence of SINS are thermoregulation and inappropriate water supply, stress, genetics, and inflammatory response to lipopolysaccharides (mainly from Escherichia coli). Animals afected by SINS may experience pain and discomfort due to vasculitis and thrombosis of the vessels, decreasing the animal welfare. The present case report describes the first time an outbreak of SINS outside Europe and the associated severe lesions in suckling piglets.
answer: Swine Inflammation and Necrosis Syndrome (SINS) causes inflammation and necrotic lesions in acral areas of pigs, especially the tail, ears, coronary bands, heels, soles, claw wall, teats, vulva, umbilicus, and face. It can affect suckling, weaned, and fattening pigs, with suckling piglet signs most evident in the first week of life and progressing from bristle loss to swelling, redness, exudation, and necrosis. SINS is associated with feed mycotoxins, inadequate thermoregulation or water supply, stress, genetics, and inflammatory responses to lipopolysaccharides, and it reduces welfare through pain, vasculitis, and thrombosis; this case report describes the first outbreak outside Europe.

query: CMPs are the most common heart diseases in cats, with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy being the most prevalent phenotype. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype (HCM-Ph) is characterised by left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) without chamber dilation. Secondary causes in cats include systemic hypertension, hyperthyroidism, aortic stenosis, acromegaly, neoplasia, transient myocardial thickening (TMT) and dehydration. Infectious myocarditis can also cause secondary LVH in cats, with several agents implicated. The most commonly implicated pathogens are viruses, including feline Coronavirus, feline immunodeficiency virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome Coronavirus 2. Other infectious agents, including Toxoplasma gondii and Bartonella henselae, have also been identified. However, in the majority of LVH cases, no underlying cause can be found; in such cases, the term “hypertrophic cardiomyopathy” (HCM) is used instead. It is worth noting that causative mutations encoding sarcomeric proteins have been identified in Maine Coon, Ragdoll and Sphynx cats. Several other genetic variants have also been associated with HCM in Bengal cats, Domestic Shorthair cats and Birman cats. However, a definitive causal link with the disease has yet to be established for these breeds. Most research in the feline literature has focused on HCM, reporting a prevalence of 15% in the general feline population, reaching 29% in older cats. At the same time, several other studies have also addressed HCM-Ph, reporting an overall prevalence ranging from 8% to 34%.
answer: Cardiomyopathies are the most common feline heart diseases, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype (HCM-Ph) is defined by left ventricular hypertrophy without chamber dilation. Secondary feline LVH can result from disorders such as hypertension, hyperthyroidism, aortic stenosis, acromegaly, neoplasia, transient myocardial thickening, dehydration, or infectious myocarditis caused by agents including feline Coronavirus, FIV, SARS-CoV-2, Toxoplasma gondii, and Bartonella henselae; when no cause is found, it is termed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Feline HCM has genetic associations in several breeds, with causal sarcomeric mutations identified in Maine Coon, Ragdoll, and Sphynx cats, and reported prevalence around 15% generally, 29% in older cats, and 8%–34% for HCM-Ph.

query: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma is a rare vascular neoplasm, particularly in non-human species, and this represents the first documented case involving the alimentary tract in animals. Here, we report the clinicopathological features, immunohistochemical profile, and one-year treatment outcome of a feline gastroduodenal junction KHE. We also showed that ERG and Cav-1 may serve as a potential alternative tool for the immunohistochemical diagnosis of vascular neoplasms in cats. Vascular tumors should be considered in the diferential diagnosis of gastrointestinal masses in cats, given their potential for locally aggressive behavior and associated complications.
answer: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma is a rare vascular tumor in non-human species, and this feline gastroduodenal junction case is reported as the first documented alimentary-tract case in animals. The report describes clinicopathological, immunohistochemical, and one-year outcome findings, suggests ERG and Cav-1 as potential immunohistochemical markers for feline vascular neoplasms, and recommends considering vascular tumors among differential diagnoses for gastrointestinal masses in cats.

query: APPs are commonly used in veterinary medicine to tackle systemic inflammatory processes, but their diagnostic value in various feline respiratory diseases has not yet been investigated. This study examined the APPs SAA and Hp in cats with diferent respiratory diseases and investigated the association with clinical signs and shortterm outcome. It was shown that cats with infectious lower airway or pleural space disease had higher, but not necessarily increased, levels of APPs in comparison to patients with other respiratory diseases. In contrast to other respiratory diseases, cats with FLAD had lower levels of APPs. In addition, most APP values were within the respective reference range despite presence of respiratory disease. It therefore does not appear possible to diferentiate between various respiratory conditions on the basis of serum APP levels, and APP levels in the reference range cannot rule out ongoing respiratory disease.
answer: This study evaluated serum acute phase proteins SAA and Hp in cats with different respiratory diseases, including their associations with clinical signs and short-term outcome. Cats with infectious lower airway or pleural space disease had higher APP levels than cats with other respiratory diseases, while cats with FLAD had lower levels, but most values remained within reference ranges. Serum APP concentrations therefore could not reliably distinguish feline respiratory conditions, and normal APP values did not rule out respiratory disease.

query: Hepatic lipidosis is the condition in which lipid alterations are most consistently described in cats. Across multiple studies, characteristic features include triacylglycerol accumulation, altered VLDL handling, changes in LDL and HDL composition, and modifications in sphingolipid profiles. These findings collectively suggest a disruption of hepatic lipid trafficking processes rather than a single isolated metabolic defect. Nevertheless, mechanistic interpretation should remain cautious. While several pathways—such as impaired lipoprotein export, altered fatty acid flux, and regulatory limitations in VLDL metabolism—are supported by feline data, broader interpretations often rely on extrapolation from other species and general lipid biology. Accordingly, hepatic lipidosis represents the most robust example of disease-associated lipid remodeling in cats, but not yet a fully resolved mechanistic framework.
answer: Hepatic lipidosis is the feline disease with the most consistently described lipid alterations, including triacylglycerol accumulation, altered VLDL handling, changes in LDL and HDL composition, and sphingolipid profile modifications. These changes suggest disrupted hepatic lipid trafficking involving impaired lipoprotein export, altered fatty acid flux, and limits in VLDL metabolism, although the full mechanism remains unresolved and partly extrapolated from other species.

query: We describe the first large animal model of FXS in the development of two founder sheep, a ram and a ewe, carrying loss-of-function mutations in the FMR1 gene. A CRISPR-Cas9 approach was undertaken using a dual guide to disrupt the translation start (MET) codon and delete 45 bp from exon one. The founder ewe carried the expected deletion on one allele and one- and two-base-pair deletions at the guide-mediated cut sites on the other allele. This, in effect, inactivated both alleles, resulting in no FMRP evident in the tail tissue. The ram carried a single deletion of 2706 bp, cleaving one bp upstream of the Met codon and a deletion incorporating all of exon one and 2653 bp into intron one. The large deletion resulted in no FMR1 mRNA and, consequently, no FMRP as measured in the tail tissue.
answer: The first large-animal model of Fragile X Syndrome was generated in sheep by using CRISPR-Cas9 dual guides to disrupt the FMR1 translation start codon and exon one. The founder ewe had biallelic FMR1-inactivating edits and no detectable FMRP in tail tissue, while the founder ram carried a 2706 bp deletion removing exon one and extending into intron one, resulting in no FMR1 mRNA or FMRP in tail tissue.

query: Bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in pre-weaned calves, yet the role of commensal nasal microbiota in outbreak severity remains poorly understood. This study characterized nasal bacterial communities during two BRDC outbreaks of differing severity (moderate vs. severe) and at \~30 days post-treatment. Nasal swabs were collected from calves and analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V1–V3 regions, Illumina MiSeq) and quantitative PCR targeting three major BRDC pathogens. Microbial community profiles differed between outbreak groups and across timepoints. Calves in the severe outbreak group exhibited lower microbial diversity compared to those in the moderate outbreak. In both groups, diversity significantly increased from outbreak to post-treatment. At the time of disease, nasal communities were dominated by the genera Mycoplasmopsis, Mesomycoplasma, and Caviibacter, with qPCR confirming Mycoplasma bovirhinis as the predominant species. These findings indicate that BRDC outbreaks in pre-weaned calves are associated with reduced microbial diversity and the dominance of pathogenic Mycoplasma species, with recovery characterized by greater bacterial diversity. Shifts in nasal microbiome composition between outbreak and post-treatment may reflect pathogen-driven disruption during disease and subsequent microbial community rebalancing.
answer: In pre-weaned calves, BRDC outbreaks were associated with reduced nasal microbial diversity, especially in the severe outbreak group, and diversity increased by about 30 days after treatment. During disease, nasal communities were dominated by Mycoplasmopsis, Mesomycoplasma, and Caviibacter, with qPCR identifying Mycoplasma bovirhinis as the predominant species, suggesting pathogen-driven dysbiosis followed by microbial rebalancing during recovery.

query: Inflammatory cytokines and haptoglobin (HPT) were measured from 28 head of cattle that presented with bovine respiratory disease after being purchased and shipped to a common feedlot and assigned to either control or metaphylaxis treatment groups. Blood samples were obtained on the day of purchase (D0) and again at the time of diagnosis (S0) and 5 days after treatment (S5). Plasma was harvested and stored at −80 °C until assayed for the cytokines IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and HPT. Our objectives in this study were to determine diferences between baseline (D0), day of diagnosis (S0) and post-treatment (S5), as well as to identify correlations among cytokine and HPT concentrations over time and by treatment. Interferon-gamma and IL-1β concentrations did not difer between D0 and S0 or S5. Tumor necrosis factor-α concentrations difered between D0 and both S0 and S5; however, no diferences were observed between S0 and S5. Interleukin-6 and HPT concentrations difered between D0 and S0, D0 and S5, and between S0 and S5. Neither control nor metaphylactic treatment significantly impacted cytokine or HPT concentrations, nor did the state of origin. The strongest significant correlations among cytokine-timepoint combinations were observed for IL-1β and TNF-α S0 (0.93), and S5 (0.91). Both IL-6 and HPT increased from baseline to the time of BRD diagnosis and treatment, and HPT exhibited the most rapid decline after treatment (S5), suggesting that it may be the most useful single measurement for indicating both sickness and resolution post-treatment.
answer: In 28 feedlot cattle with bovine respiratory disease, cytokines and haptoglobin (HPT) were measured at purchase (D0), diagnosis/treatment (S0), and 5 days after treatment (S5). IFN-γ and IL-1β did not change across time points, TNF-α differed from baseline but not between S0 and S5, while IL-6 and HPT differed among all time points; treatment group, metaphylaxis, and state of origin had no significant effects. IL-6 and HPT increased at BRD diagnosis, and HPT declined most rapidly after treatment, suggesting it may be the most useful single marker for both sickness and post-treatment resolution.

query: The upper respiratory tract is composed of the nares, nasal passages, and choana. While the nares of most reptiles are simple openings to allow passage of air, some species have unique adaptations. Marine iguanas (Amblyrhynchus cristatus) have a slight extension of tissue beyond the nasal opening to help expel salt from their salt glands. The most complex nares are found in crocodilians. They possess musculature, the constrictor naris and dilator naris, that allow voluntary closing and opening of the nares, respectively. This adaptation is likely because crocodilians are the only reptile group to have a secondary bony palate (often termed the hard palate in mammals) and pharyngeal choana as opposed to a choanal opening in the oral cavity. They also have a palatal valve that further seals the pharyngeal cavity when underwater. This valve blocks the flow of water that would otherwise go directly into the glottis and esophagus. The muscular nares, together with the ability to seal the nasal passages through engorgement of the vascular cavernous tissue, allow crocodilians to prevent the intrusion of water through the nasal passages when underwater. Nasal conchae are simpler structures than in mammals and are absent in chelonians. Instead, the nasal cavities of chelonians have a series of non-bony diverticula.
answer: The reptile upper respiratory tract consists of the nares, nasal passages, and choana, with adaptations varying by taxon. Marine iguanas have tissue extensions near the nares that help expel salt, while crocodilians have the most complex nares, using constrictor and dilator muscles, a secondary bony palate, pharyngeal choana, palatal valve, and vascular cavernous tissue to seal the airway and prevent water entry underwater. Reptile nasal conchae are simpler than in mammals and are absent in chelonians, whose nasal cavities instead contain non-bony diverticula.

query: Mares can experience significant nociceptive pain during the postpartum period, even after normal foaling. This pain mainly results from swelling and irritation of the birth canal and muscle soreness due to the exertion of labor. Importantly, dystocia or postpartum complications such as birth canal injuries, retained fetal membranes, laminitis, mastitis, or post-foaling colic can greatly exacerbate the pain. Accurate assessment and management of pain in these cases are critical for animal welfare and guiding timely and appropriate analgesic interventions. Unrelieved pain can provoke excessive sympathetic nervous system activation, metabolic disturbances, and immunosuppression, which together increase morbidity and impede recovery. Because pain intensity cannot be measured directly in animals, veterinarians rely on indirect evaluation methods such as behavioral pain scales. An effective pain scale defines specific behavioral and physiological criteria tailored to the species, enabling the detection of even subtle changes in the animal’s appearance or vital signs that may indicate pain. To ensure the tool is scientifically sound and clinically useful, it must undergo validation with respect to key psychometric properties such as reliability and validity. An important aspect of validation is comparison of the new scale’s scores with an independent indicator of pain, like cortisol levels. Cortisol is a stress hormone known to increase in response to pain in equids, as a result of HPA axis activation (CRH→ACTH→adrenal cortex). Cortisol passively diffuses from blood into the saliva, and salivary cortisol largely mirrors free cortisol with a short lag. Measuring cortisol in saliva is noninvasive because it only requires putting a cotton swab or a Salivette® into a horse’s mouth; therefore, it should not increase the preexisting pain.
answer: Postpartum mares can have nociceptive pain from birth-canal swelling, irritation, and muscle soreness, with dystocia or complications such as birth canal injuries, retained fetal membranes, laminitis, mastitis, and post-foaling colic worsening pain. Because animal pain cannot be measured directly, veterinarians use species-specific behavioral and physiological pain scales that require validation for reliability and validity. Salivary cortisol is a noninvasive validation marker in equids because pain activates the HPA axis, cortisol rises, and free cortisol diffuses into saliva with a short lag.

query: Although the highest observed agreement for S neurona antibody detection was between ELISA and WB (83.3%), the corresponding κ value (0.36) indicated only “fair agreement,” suggesting that the apparent concordance was largely due to chance rather than consistent classification of samples. Agreement between IFAT and ELISA was numerically moderate (77.6%), but the κ value was very low (0.08), reflecting “minimal agreement beyond chance.” Agreement between IFAT and WB was even poorer (40.0%; κ = 0.05). For N hughesi, the agreement between IFAT and ELISA was high in absolute terms (82.8%) but the κ value was slightly negative ( 0.03), confirming “no meaningful concordance” between assays. Overall, despite seemingly moderate or high raw agreement percentages, the κ statistics clearly indicate that these tests perform inconsistently and classify samples diferently. This poor concordance likely reflects diferences in antigen targets and analytical methods among assays, and reinforces that the serological tests for S neurona and N hughesi cannot be used interchangeably for diagnostic or epidemiologic purposes. In addition, this reinforces that serological testing alone should not be used to make a diagnosis of EPM and use of serum:CSF titer ratios should be considered.
answer: Serological assays for equine protozoal myeloencephalitis pathogens showed poor concordance despite moderate or high raw agreement percentages: for S neurona, ELISA-WB agreement was 83.3% but only fair by kappa (κ = 0.36), IFAT-ELISA was 77.6% with minimal agreement beyond chance (κ = 0.08), and IFAT-WB was 40.0% (κ = 0.05). For N hughesi, IFAT-ELISA agreement was 82.8% but had no meaningful concordance by kappa (κ = 0.03), indicating these tests should not be used interchangeably and serology alone should not diagnose EPM; serum:CSF titer ratios should be considered.

query: Temperature extremes, both acute and chronic, significantly impair the immune functions of fish, reducing their ability to combat pathogens. One of the primary features of immune responses to temperature stress is the elevation of antibody levels. Serum lysozyme (LSZ) activities are vital innate immune defense molecules in teleosts responsible for breaking down the cell walls of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Lysozyme is opsonic, activating the complement system and promoting phagocytosis. Immunoglobulins (Ig) or antibodies, which play a vital role in adaptive immune responses, are heterodimeric glycoproteins belonging to the broad Ig superfamily $\mathrm { ( I g S F ) }$ with Immunoglobulin M (IgM) being the most predominant found in fish. Hepcidin, a cysteine-rich antimicrobial peptide produced and secreted by the liver during inflammation, plays a key role in antimicrobial defense. Furthermore, interleukin (IL)-1β and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) are significant mediators of the inflammatory response in fish. For example, turbot (Scophthalmus maximus) exposed to high temperatures $( 2 0 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }, 2 3 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }, 2 5 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }, 2 7 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C },$ and $2 8 ~ ^ { \circ } C )$ resulted in a significant increase in mucus immunity, including IgM, IL-1β, hepcidin, transferrin, LSZ, and acid/alkaline phosphatase. Another study reported a significant decrease in LSZ activity in Nile tilapia reared at $3 3 ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ after 4 weeks of exposure. Significantly increased plasma IgM and LSZ were also reported for olive flounder exposed at 28 and $3 0 ~ ^ { \circ } \mathrm { C }$ for 2 weeks.
answer: Acute and chronic temperature extremes impair fish immunity and pathogen resistance, with responses involving antibody elevation and innate and inflammatory mediators such as lysozyme, IgM, hepcidin, IL-1β, and TNF-α. High-temperature exposure increased mucus immune factors in turbot at 20–28 °C and increased plasma IgM and lysozyme in olive flounder at 28 and 30 °C for 2 weeks, while Nile tilapia held at 33 °C for 4 weeks showed decreased lysozyme activity.

query: Te avian immune system includes both innate immunities, serving as the initial defense, and adaptive immunity, involving T and B cells that mediate cellular and humoral responses to antigens, respectively. B cells produce antibodies, and the three types of antibodies found in chicken are IgM, IgA and IgG. Heat stress can reduce the immune response in poultry by decreasing the size and functionality of immune organs like the spleen, thymus, and bursa. Tis shrinkage occurs because heat stress elevates circulating glucocorticoids, which suppress lymphocyte proliferation, promote apoptosis, and cause morphological damage in lymphoid tissues such as the thymus and bursa, leading to atrophy. Tis reduction in organ function can lead to increased susceptibility to infections and diminished overall health in afected chicken. Consequently, the incidence of infectious poultry diseases like Newcastle disease tends to be higher during the summer in tropical regions.
answer: Chickens rely on innate immunity and adaptive immunity mediated by T and B cells, with B cells producing IgM, IgA, and IgG antibodies. Heat stress suppresses poultry immunity by raising circulating glucocorticoids, which reduce lymphocyte proliferation, promote apoptosis, and damage lymphoid organs such as the spleen, thymus, and bursa, causing atrophy. This weakened immune function increases infection susceptibility and is linked to higher summer incidence of diseases such as Newcastle disease in tropical regions.

query: In this study, we directly compared lung histopathology between severity-matched SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus (IAV) infection models and found that comparable overall inflammatory burden can mask pathogen-specific differences in the spatial organization and qualitative character of lung injury and recovery. Despite similar aggregate inflammation scores, the two viruses differed in lesion topology, epithelial tropism, local inflammatorycell composition, and the architecture of residual lesions during the resolution phase. SARS-CoV-2 more frequently involved broader interstitial and alveolar compartments during the peak-injury phase and transitioned toward localized residual inflammatory foci, whereas IAV showed more bronchocentric acute lesions followed by more conspicuous remodeling-associated changes during the resolution phase. These distinctions support the view that, for experimental viral pneumonia, lesion distribution and residual structural organization represent key dimensions of interpretation that are not fully captured by burden-based grading alone. This interpretation is consistent with prior pathology literature showing that severe viral pneumonias may share major injury categories while still differing in lesion localization, compartmental involvement, and remodeling context.
answer: Severity-matched SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus lung infection models can show similar overall inflammation scores while differing in lesion distribution, epithelial tropism, inflammatory-cell composition, and residual lesion architecture. SARS-CoV-2 lesions more often involved interstitial and alveolar compartments at peak injury and later became localized residual inflammatory foci, whereas IAV caused more bronchocentric acute lesions followed by more prominent remodeling during resolution. These differences show that burden-based grading alone may miss important pathogen-specific patterns in experimental viral pneumonia.

query: From an ecological epidemiology perspective, wildlife nasal cavities may serve as critical ecological niches for the maintenance and spread of bacterial pathogens relevant to both animal and human health. This study investigated Streptococcus spp. as the most prevalent genus in the nasal cavities of 82 wild boars (Sus scrofa), sampled across six hunting districts in Avellino Province (Southern Italy), assessing the diversity of the colonizing streptococcal populations and their antimicrobial resistance profiles. The sampled population consisted of 43 males (52%) and 39 females (48%). A total of 173 Gram-positive isolates were recovered, with 74 identified as Streptococcus spp. by MALDI-TOF MS. These isolates originated from 59 positive swabs (72%; 59/82). Streptococcus gallolyticus was the most prevalent species (41%; 30/74), followed by Streptococcus porcinus (27%; 20/74) and Streptococcus suis (19%; 14/74). No statistically significant geographic association was found across sampling districts $( p = 0. 4 9 1 )$, whereas a significant association was found between bacterial species and antimicrobial resistance profiles $( \chi ^ { 2 } = 1 6. 7 0, p < 0. 0 0 1 )$. Specifically, all Streptococcus porcinus isolates (100%; 20/20) exhibited resistance to sulfamethoxazole–trimethoprim and tetracycline, while high tetracycline resistance was also noted in Streptococcus suis (93%; 13/14) and Streptococcus gallolyticus (83%; 25/30). Overall, 69% (51/74) of isolates were classified as MDR and 5% (4/74) as XDR. These findings suggest the potential role of wild boars as reservoirs for antimicrobial-resistant streptococci, emphasizing the need for continuous surveillance under a One Health framework.
answer: In 82 wild boars from six districts in Avellino Province, Southern Italy, 74 Streptococcus isolates were identified from 59 positive nasal swabs, mainly Streptococcus gallolyticus, Streptococcus porcinus, and Streptococcus suis. Resistance profiles differed significantly by bacterial species, with all S. porcinus isolates resistant to sulfamethoxazole–trimethoprim and tetracycline, high tetracycline resistance in S. suis and S. gallolyticus, and 69% of isolates classified as MDR and 5% as XDR, supporting wild boars as potential One Health reservoirs of antimicrobial-resistant streptococci.

query: AMR represents one of the most pressing threats to animal and public health worldwide. In poultry production, pathogens such as Salmonella enterica serovars continue to exhibit resistance to commonly used antibiotics, undermining both disease control and food safety. Similarly, in dairy systems, mastitiscausing pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and multidrug-resistant streptococci, have reduced the efectiveness of conventional therapies while increasing the risk of antibiotic residues in milk. A unifying theme across the articles is the urgent need to reduce dependence on traditional antibiotics without compromising animal welfare or production eficiency. In poultry and dairy systems alike, the irrational or prophylactic use of antimicrobials has driven the emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens such as Salmonella spp., Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus uberis, and Streptococcus dysgalactiae. The studies highlighted in this Research Topic directly address this challenge by evaluating ethnomedicinal interventions that exert antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory efects through multiple, often synergistic mechanisms. Unlike the traditional antibiotics, which typically act on single pathogen targets, plant-derived bioactive compounds and traditional formulations often exhibit broad spectrum of action that influence a network of biological pathways. This includes modulation of host immune responses, reinforcement of epithelial barrier integrity, alteration of gut or mammary microbiota composition, and suppression of pathogen virulence factors. Such multi-target efects reduce the likelihood of resistance development while simultaneously improving host resilience to infection.
answer: Antimicrobial resistance threatens animal and public health in poultry and dairy systems, with resistant Salmonella enterica in poultry and mastitis pathogens such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and multidrug-resistant streptococci reducing treatment effectiveness and raising food safety concerns. Ethnomedicinal interventions are being evaluated as alternatives to overused antibiotics because plant-derived compounds and traditional formulations can exert antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory effects through multiple pathways, including immune modulation, epithelial barrier support, microbiota alteration, and suppression of pathogen virulence. These broad, multi-target actions may lower resistance development while improving host resilience to infection.

query: Antibiotic use in livestock drives selection before pathogens ever reach humans. Metaphylactic administration of ceftiofur in poultry has been shown to drive a dramatic increase in resistance, with the proportion of Salmonella Heidelberg isolates resistant to thirdgeneration cephalosporins rising from approximately 5% to 35% over a single production cycle, a trend mirrored by parallel increases in human clinical cases. These findings underscore the importance of enforcing strict withdrawal periods to prevent antimicrobial residues from entering the food chain, as well as the implementation of regulatory frameworks that limit the non-therapeutic use of critically important antimicrobials in foodproducing animals. Likewise, subtherapeutic dosing of florfenicol in calves not only enriched intestinal Escherichia coli populations harboring multidrug-resistance plasmids but also disrupted short-chain fatty acid profiles, thereby compromising animal health and creating reservoirs with zoonotic potential. In plant agriculture, routine sprays of streptomycin and tetracycline on fruit orchards elevated the prevalence of streptomycin resistant Pseudomonas syringae to over 40% within leaf-surface microbiomes, illustrating a feedback loop whereby agricultural use of antibiotics propagates resistance that can cycle back into animal and human populations.
answer: Antibiotic use in agriculture can select for antimicrobial resistance before pathogens reach humans: ceftiofur use in poultry increased third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Salmonella Heidelberg from about 5% to 35% in one production cycle, alongside increases in human clinical cases. Subtherapeutic florfenicol in calves enriched multidrug-resistant intestinal Escherichia coli and altered short-chain fatty acid profiles, while streptomycin and tetracycline sprays in orchards raised streptomycin-resistant Pseudomonas syringae above 40%, supporting withdrawal periods and limits on non-therapeutic use of critical antimicrobials.

query: Klebsiella pneumoniae is an important emerging pathogen leading to serious clinical outcomes as the multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates arise. While K. pneumoniae is a well-known pathogen in human clinical settings, its risks in nonhuman hosts and potential for cross-species transmission remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed whole-genome sequencing on– 112 K. pneumoniae isolates from four host sources in Northeast China to elucidate their phylogenetic relationships and charac-– – – terize their antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and virulence profiles. Our analysis identified 53 distinct sequence types (STs), 38 Klocus (KL) types, and nine O-loci. Notably, several strains with identical ST KL combinations were shared across different hosts: ST76 KL5 was detected in both human and dairy cow sources; ST412 KL57 was found in human and chicken; ST111 KL63 was present in both pig and dairy cow sources, suggesting potential interspecies transmission. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) showed that nearly all human- and pig-derived isolates were resistant to β-lactams, quinolones, co-trimoxazole, tetracyclines, and at least one aminoglycoside.
